summary.text: Nicole Malliotakis is the Republican and Conservative Party incumbent in New York's 11th Congressional District, which covers Staten Island and part of southern Brooklyn. A Staten Island native, she worked as a public affairs professional and for state officials before serving in the New York State Assembly from 2011 to 2021, running for mayor of New York City in 2017, and winning her House seat in 2020. She sits on the House Ways and Means Committee and the Joint Economic Committee and is seeking a fourth term.

paragraphs.text: Born on November 11, 1980, in Manhattan; moved to Staten Island at age two and grew up in the Great Kills neighborhood.
Graduated from New Dorp High School in 1998, earned a B.A. in communications from Seton Hall University in 2001, and earned an M.B.A. from Wagner College in 2010.

Worked as a community liaison for State Senator John Marchi (2003–2004) and for Governor George Pataki (2004–2006), and later as a public affairs manager at Consolidated Edison, before entering elected office.

Won election to the New York State Assembly in 2010 by defeating incumbent Democrat Janele Hyer-Spencer, and represented District 60 (2011–2013) and District 64 (2013–2021). Wikipedia reports she was the first Greek-American woman and first Cuban-American woman elected to office in New York State.
Was the Republican nominee for mayor of New York City in 2017 and lost to incumbent Democrat Bill de Blasio, 66% to 28%.
Won the 11th Congressional District seat in 2020, defeating incumbent Democrat Max Rose, 53% to 47%; was re-elected in 2022 over Rose and in 2024 over Democrat Andrea Morse.

Named to the House Committee on Ways and Means in January 2023. In the 119th Congress she sits on the Ways and Means Subcommittees on Tax and on Oversight and on the Joint Economic Committee, and is an Assistant Whip for the House Republican Conference; in the 117th Congress she served on the Foreign Affairs and Transportation and Infrastructure Committees.
According to her House website, she is Co-Chair of the Congressional Anti-Congestion Tax Caucus, Vice Chair of the Problem Solvers Caucus and Vice Chair of the Congressional Hellenic Caucus.

Sponsored H.R. 9499, the Protecting Taxpayers from Ghost Preparers Act, which her office says passed the House unanimously, and H.R. 5439, the Medically Tailored Home-Delivered Meals Program Pilot Act with Rep. James McGovern, which advanced from the Ways and Means Committee.
